_: The camera's knobs (camera_rig.gd reads them; one owner). floor: the closest the lens comes, a low oblique just over the roofs (Mac: no close-up realism). go_to: the distance each kind of 'go to X' frames at (the one framing rule, camera_rig.go_to; Anno 1800 / Manor Lords jump). sight_steps: how many headings either way go_to tries before taking the least blocked. near_fade: what stands right in front of the lens dissolves (Godot's dithered distance fade; Anno 1800 / Manor Lords): gone nearer than 'gone', whole from 'solid', in game units from the lens; buildings, trees and a castle's walls each (a castle's go sooner: wide and tall, at roof height they would fill the foreground). doubleClick (camera_rig.gd double_click; Total War's campaign map, CK3, Google Maps): a left double-click on the ground eases the view's aim onto that spot and comes step of the distance closer (0.35: 20 -> 13), never under the floor; at the floor it only re-centres. The ease is the rig's own (EASE 9 a second: most of the way in about a third of a second).

shots._: The director's own shots (director.gd; the professional audit: one gate-and-banner framing reused for every scene): each new shot turns from the last by one of these (radians), never the same turn twice running, and its distance varies by up to this share either way. The sight rule (sight_steps) still has the last word.

town_view._: The town view you start with (focus round 2: d19 showed the whole town, the lake and Eaglehaven, the square 12% of the frame's width; 01-town is close: the square about 40% across, six to eight houses, the castle's gate and keep filling the upper right. dist 6 is the floor (the closest the player's lens comes): the square 37% across, the castle's foot upper right, its top past the frame's top, as 01-town; frame probe --frame-probe=sweep) (main._home_view, the Z key; autoplay's home step; docs/review/focus.sh; camera_rig.town_view; art target 01-town): the square in the middle, the castle behind it to the upper right, houses all round, the wall and fields beyond. dist (camera units), pitch (degrees down; docs/research/quality-deep-dive.md #1: RTS town cameras sit at 40-60 degrees and 01-town reads 40-45, so 40 here and at the film's closer frame; camera_rig.town_view sets it as the view's tilt over the rig's own pitch for that distance, so zooming in from it keeps the tilt: about 35-37 down at the floor, under clarity.maxPitch), ahead (the aim this share of the distance past the square, away from the lens, so the square stands in the lower middle as in 01-town: frame probe, the square at 0.62 down), castle_x (where the castle stands: 0 the middle, 1 the right edge), castle_turn_most (radians the heading may turn from the side away from the castle to put it there).

town_shot._: A town's square framed for a still (the shot harness's --city; camera_rig.square_view; art target 01-town): away_from_castle (1: the lens on the far side of the square from the castle, so the castle stands behind it; 0: the old fixed heading), turn (radians off that line, so the castle sits to one side), card_shift (the square set right of the middle by this share of the distance, clear of the town card on the left).

clarity._: The player always sees clearly what he looks at (Mac, 2026-11-12: 'I can barely see anything'; Age of Empires IV and Anno 1800 town cameras: no near blur, the lens never in or behind a building, a crisp foreground). on (or --clarity=on; --clarity=old for the before shot): the pitch is the player's or the step's; a roof in the line, the view first swings swingStep degrees either way, up to swingTries steps, to a clear line; failing that it lifts liftStep degrees at a time, at most liftTries steps and never past maxPitch degrees down (batch 8: an unlimited lift made every town shot top-down); then it comes in short of the roof, but never nearer than nearest of its distance (batch 8: d14 collapsed to 6); the sight check also keeps the frame's lower third clear of buildings and street things near the lens (lines to the ground lowerAt of the way to the focus, lowerSide of the distance either side; a hit in the near lowerNear of a line counts); all eased at liftEase a second; and what stands at the lens dissolves only within fade.gone..fade.solid (game units), instead of near_fade's wider ghosting.

frame._: The clear frame bottom (batch 9: a ghosted house down the right quarter of Kingsmere, near roofs and chimney pots over the bottom third at d4.5-6). Age of Empires IV's and Anno 1800's closest town zoom: the camera stands over open ground with the frame's bottom clear, and nothing is cut away or see-through. on (0: batch 9's lower-third lines, lowerAt..lowerNear). Rays through a 6x3 grid over the frame's bottom third (aspect: the film's width over height) count what a building, a street thing or a tree's crown (forest.gd's sight lines, as roofs) fills nearer than within of the way to the aim; a frame is clean at allow or less, with no roof or crown on the line to the aim and nothing within gap of the lens (fade.solid is 1.0: nearer, it would ghost). Not clean: the smallest change that is, in order: a swing (swingStep, swingTries), the lens and its aim raised together over the roof line (riseStep of the distance but at least riseLeast units, riseTries; Anno 1800's pivot over the rooftops: the pitch kept, the ground a little lower in the frame), the lens in along its arm (shortStep of the arm, shortTries), a lift (liftStep, liftTries, never past maxPitch), then swings with each rise; none clean, the least bad. Re-chosen when the lens or aim moves or every hold seconds; eased at liftEase.

smoke._: Chimney smoke near the lens fades out (hearths.gd; the smoke material's distance fade): gone nearer than 'gone', whole from 'solid', in game units from the lens (batch 9: smoke drifting across the near houses at d6).

labels._: An inn's name (roads.gd, roadside.gd): set 'over' above the top of its own roofs within 'reach' of it, and hidden while a building stands between it and the lens (camera_rig, checked every 'every' seconds) instead of being cut by a roof.

map._: The mid and map zoom (art target 02-realm; Warcraft III's RTS camera, CK3's map switch). atlas_from / atlas_to: the camera distance over which the flat painted atlas comes in over the 3D land, and atlas_most how far it goes (the painted overview, realm_map.gd, takes over past camera_rig OVERVIEW, 60): below atlas_from the 3D land is all there is. reach: how far from the lens a town's kit models still draw (towns.gd _reach_for), by size: clutter (under 2 m), small (under 6 m), house (under 15 m), great (under 25 m: halls, churches), castle (anything larger, and a castle or landmark placed whole); Godot's own generated detail levels (realistic.gd _merge) lighten them with distance, so a town far off is its same houses, lighter, never nothing.
